# DECISIONS (ADR log)

Newest first. Format: **what** — why (date). Seeded by inference from the codebase (no git history exists).

## 2026-08-20 — Roadmap-V2 E1 (list framework)
- **E1 parsers are additive on `lib/list.ts`; existing pages stay on `parseListParams`/`pageInfo(total, page)`** — `pageInfo` gained an optional 3rd `size` defaulting to `PAGE_SIZE` (20). Selectable sizes are {10,25,50,100}; 20 is the implicit default until a page opts into `PageSizeSelect`, so the E3 sweep can land page-by-page without a mass rewrite. (2026-08-20)
- **Column filters compose with FilterBar/ScorecardTiles via Prisma `AND`, they do not replace `?status=`** — the leads exemplar keeps both `?status=` and `?f_status=` so a later page can adopt column filters without ripping out its existing facet UI. Filters only key Prisma scalars (owner is toggleable, not filterable in v1 — it's a relation). (2026-08-20)
- **SavedSearch.params is opaque JSON; actions never interpret it** — `currentParamsToJson` allow-lists per page, `savedParamsToQuery` hydrates a `?…` href. Malformed JSON degrades to `?` (no 500). Unique is `tenantId+module+name`, so overwrite of a shared vs owned name is an explicit CEO/owner check. Shared views (`ownerId=null`) are CEO-only. Bare list URLs never auto-redirect to `isDefault` — a chip is offered instead. (2026-08-20)

## 2026-07-12 — Roadmap-V2 Wave D (ecosystem bridge)
- **Connector auth = per-tenant random token, stored as sha256 hash, presented via x-connector-key; tenant derived ONLY from the matched ConnectorState row** — plaintext shown once at generation (no plaintext at rest, unlike the older env-secret pattern GAPS flags); lookup-by-hash + timingSafeEqual belt-and-suspenders. Spec of record: docs/ai/design/wave-d-contracts.md. (2026-07-12)
- **Telephony/WhatsApp webhooks authenticate via `?token=` shared secret (timing-safe), not HMAC** — Exotel passthru/status callbacks are unsigned, so a signature scheme isn't available; token-in-URL is the documented provider pattern. Both webhooks are single-writer surfaces with idempotency guards (Call upsert by providerCallId + emit-once terminal; MessageLog monotonic status upgrades). Telephony resolves tenant via findFirst — same single-tenant debt class as the marketplace webhook, logged in GAPS.md. (2026-07-12)
- **Call.status / MessageLog.deliveryStatus are provider-domain literal sets, NOT Studio picklists** — they normalize external provider states at the seam (like Invoice.status); tenant-semantic vocabulary stays config-driven. (2026-07-12)
- **Tally voucher push uses XML (not TallyPrime 7 JSON) with env-configurable tax ledger names** — XML works on every TallyPrime version in the field; ledger names (Output CGST etc.) vary per chart, so TALLY_LEDGER_* envs with sensible defaults. Invoices push once (tallyPushedAt stamp + per-voucher ack), Draft invoices never push. (2026-07-12)

## 2026-07-12 — Roadmap-V2 Wave C (Service & AMC)
- **Contract/SLA automation executes directly in /api/cron, not via Job rows** — lib/jobs.ts's handler registry is dormant scaffolding (nothing ever calls scheduleJob, grep-verified), so the cron route sweeps every tenant directly each hit; the contract.renewal Job handler shares the same lib/contracts-automation.ts implementation for whenever Job scheduling becomes real. (2026-07-12)
- **PMS visit tickets are created one-per-sweep (sequential walk), not all-overdue-at-once** — a contract activated mid-period would otherwise dump its whole backlog of visit tickets in one run; with a 5-min cron the catch-up is quick anyway. Renewal tickets are one-EVER per contract (subject-prefix guard). (2026-07-12)
- **SLA hours live in ticket_priority option meta ({slaHours}), edited at /studio/sla** — the same config-as-data pattern as stage probability; no new table. New tickets default to priority-based SLA (48/24/8/4) with an explicit "No SLA" opt-out — an intentional behavior change from the old manual-hours-only dropdown. (2026-07-12)
- **Industry-pack 3–6 field cap stands; the Service edition ships as platform modules, not pack fields** — C6 found it-services-amc already at the 6-field cap; rather than raising it, the vertical depth (Contracts, Installed Base, ticket types, renewal automation) is now default platform capability for every tenant, which is strictly stronger than pack-gating it. Packs stay curated. (2026-07-12)

## 2026-07-12 — Roadmap-V2 Wave B (quotation builder)
- **Quotation stages live in the new `quotation_stage` picklist (7 stages, categories open/won/lost); the original dormant `quotation_status` key stays in DEFAULT_PICKLISTS untouched** — removing it would churn existing tenants' picklist rows for zero benefit; nothing in app code ever consumed it. All quotation logic keys on `quotation_stage` categories. Prune candidate for a future config-migration story. (2026-07-12)
- **Quote→invoice reconciliation via an explicit untaxed "Round-off" invoice line** — invoice lines re-derive base as qty×rounded-unitPrice and computeGst rounds in a different order than lib/quote.ts, so stored grand totals could drift by a paise or two (caught by the B6 gate). Rather than distorting unit prices or re-plumbing computeGst, the conversion appends a Round-off line carrying the exact delta — standard Indian invoice practice, visible on the document. (2026-07-12)
- **Quotation lock rule**: `convertedInvoiceId` set → fully locked; stage in won/lost category → lines + header locked but stage may revert to an open-category value; New-revision blocked only when converted — reopening negotiation on a won/lost quote via revision is a legitimate workflow. (2026-07-12)
- **Lead-Created TAT approximates close time with `updatedAt`** — Opportunity has no closedAt column and Wave B froze schema post-B1; the stage-closing write itself bumps @updatedAt, making it the closest honest value. Revisit if a closedAt column ever lands. (2026-07-12)

- **Pluggable SSO (Google OAuth), gated on env like `lib/irp.ts`/`lib/payments.ts`; no JIT provisioning** — `lib/sso.ts` exposes `ssoConfigured` (both `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`+`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` set), `googleAuthUrl`, `exchangeCodeForProfile` (never throws, returns `null` on failure). The callback (`app/api/auth/sso/google/callback/route.ts`) only signs in an **existing, active** user matched by email — it never auto-creates an account/tenant on first Google login. Whether to auto-provision (and with what default role/tenant) is a policy decision left for a real deployment, not a technical default; a real implementation must also add CSRF `state` verification and possibly ID-token/nonce checks (documented in `lib/sso.ts` / `SSO_SETUP_DOC` and `.env.sso.example`). (2026-07-06)
- **Payments: `recordPayment` (receipt-generating) is separate from the existing `markPaidAction`** — `recordPaymentAction` writes a `Payment` row + receipt no. and flips the invoice to Paid, but `markPaidAction` is kept as a no-receipt "just settle it" path so existing UI/flows don't break. Both live in `finance/invoices/actions.ts` (finance is this agent's area). (2026-07-06)
- **Razorpay upgrade creates an order but does NOT flip the plan; manual mode flips immediately** — mirrors the mock-or-live IRP law: paid-plan activation must wait for a verified webhook signature (money-critical), so live-mode `upgradePlanAction` returns the order for checkout only. With no keys, applying the plan change directly is safe and keeps the demo usable. Webhook verification is documented in `lib/payments.ts` / `.env.payments.example` but left unbuilt. (2026-07-06)
- **Plans are a static `PLANS` registry in `lib/billing.ts`, not a DB table** — plan definitions (seats/price/features) are code; only the tenant's chosen plan is stored (on `Subscription`, denormalized onto `Tenant.plan/seats`). Seat usage derives from `count(active users)`. (2026-07-06)
- **Admin data export/delete are server actions, not `app/api/` routes** — the admin build was scoped to own only `app/(app)/admin/`; a GET route under `app/api/` would have crossed that boundary, and a server action returning a JSON string (downloaded client-side via a Blob) achieves the same "download a dump" UX without touching `app/api/`. (2026-07-06)
- **Delete-organization does explicit ordered `deleteMany` per table before deleting the `Tenant` row** — several children (Payslip, InvoiceLine, QuotationLine) already cascade via `onDelete: Cascade`, but explicit deletes make the DPDP erasure path self-documenting and robust if cascade rules change later. CEO-only, gated on typing the exact org name. (2026-07-06)
- **Modular monolith, clean-sheet (not fork ERPNext)** — keeps a single shared data model so the CEO cockpit can be truly cross-module; ERPNext fork would block the AI-native design. (2026-07-05)
- **Next.js 14 App Router, RSC-first + server actions; no separate REST layer for CRUD** — least code, colocated logic, tenant-scoping enforced server-side. (2026-07-05)
- **Multi-tenant via `tenantId` column on every table** (not schema-per-tenant) — simple for SMB scale; every query must scope by it. (2026-07-05)
- **Event bus = `EventLog` DB table + `emit()`** — powers the live cockpit/activity feed with zero infra; upgrade path to NATS/Kafka noted. (2026-07-05)
- **Provider-agnostic AI (OpenAI-compatible) with local-heuristic fallback** — runs free on Groq, swappable via `LLM_*` env, always demoable without a key. (2026-07-05)
- **Copilot classifies into 13 fixed intents; LLM never writes SQL** — safety: no arbitrary DB access from natural language. (2026-07-05)
- **Statutory maths isolated in `lib/compliance/`** — legal correctness; pure functions, unit-testable, one place to audit. (2026-07-05)
- **Pluggable IRP adapter, mock until creds** — ship the real NIC v1.1 JSON shape now; real filing needs GSP/IRP keys the owner supplies. (2026-07-05)
- **SQLite dev + Postgres prod as two synced schema files** — zero-config local dev; Prisma provider can't be an env var. (2026-07-05)
- **Hand-rolled JWT-cookie auth (jose+bcrypt), not NextAuth** — minimal deps for the MVP; flagged to revisit before production. (2026-07-05)
- **Build ignores TS/ESLint errors** (`next.config.mjs`) — velocity during parallel-agent build; trade-off: green build ≠ type-clean. (2026-07-05)

## 2026-07-11 — Orbit Studio build decisions
- **RBAC fail-closed** (deny on no-role/unknown-role/corrupt permissions; CEO bypass stays). Invites default to seeded 'Member (Full Access)' role.
- **Config-as-data**: Studio config in 9 tenant-scoped tables; custom field values in a `custom` JSON-STRING column (SQLite has no Json type — follows EventLog/Role pattern; Postgres jsonb+GIN deferred to prod migration). No EAV, no runtime DDL.
- **Category is the semantic API**: business logic (revenue-won, open-lead counts, AI scoring source weights, stage probability) keys on PicklistOption.category, never label/value literals. Enforced by convention + tests; lint rule pending WS3.
- **Atomic numbering** via NumberFormat.nextSeq increment, seeded above legacy maxima (fixes duplicate-invoice-number risk).
- **Zero-change default config**: ensureStudioDefaults() reproduces legacy hardcoded behavior exactly; pinned by unit tests.
- Repo put under git (branch studio/s0-foundations); CI workflow authored, needs GitHub remote.
